title: Investigate Sleep Fragmentation Despite Adequate Duration
description: Restless periods are elevated above your personal baseline while total sleep duration looks roughly normal — a pattern suggesting fragmented, lower-quality sleep rather than insufficient sleep. Recommends investigating likely causes rather than simply sleeping more, with relaxation practice as a secondary support.
source: Product heuristic (trigger combination); Huberman Lab (NSDR, secondary)

all.label: sleep duration >= 95% of rolling baseline (total sleep roughly normal)

conditional.question: Did you sleep a normal amount but feel like your sleep was restless or broken up?
conditional.yesLabel: Yes, help me look into possible causes
conditional.noLabel: No, that doesn't match how I slept

actions.action: Review likely fragmentation triggers from the previous evening
actions.frequency: Once, on the day this triggers
actions.details: Restlessness with otherwise-adequate sleep duration is more often explained by something specific the evening before than by a chronic problem: late alcohol (even one drink fragments sleep architecture), caffeine still active at bedtime, an unusually warm/noisy/bright bedroom, a late large meal, or elevated evening stress/screen stimulation. Reviewing the prior evening against this list is a lower-cost first step than assuming a persistent issue.

actions.action: Adjust the sleep environment and evening stimulation
actions.frequency: As needed, based on what the review above surfaces
actions.details: If a specific cause is identified (room temperature, light, noise, alcohol or caffeine timing, late high-stimulation screen use), address that specific factor rather than a generic 'sleep more' response, since total sleep time in this pattern is not the deficit.

actions.action: NSDR or brief relaxation practice before bed (secondary)
actions.details: A short NSDR or relaxation session before bed can support parasympathetic wind-down, but this is a secondary suggestion here, not the primary response — it does not address an identifiable environmental or timing cause if one exists.

benefits: Directs attention to specific, fixable causes instead of a generic 'get more sleep' response that doesn't match this pattern
Avoids over-recommending relaxation practices as a first-line fix when a concrete environmental or timing cause is more likely
Low-cost reflection step before considering anything more involved
science: Fragmented sleep (frequent restless/wake periods) with roughly preserved total sleep duration is a distinct pattern from short sleep, and is commonly associated with identifiable proximate causes — alcohol, late caffeine, an unfavorable sleep environment, or elevated pre-sleep arousal — rather than a chronic sleep-need deficit. Addressing the specific cause, where identifiable, is a more targeted response than increasing sleep opportunity, which this pattern does not actually lack.
contraindications: This is not a sleep disorder diagnosis. If restless/fragmented sleep of this kind recurs frequently (e.g. most nights over several weeks) despite addressing obvious environmental and timing factors, consider discussing with a physician, since conditions such as sleep apnea or periodic limb movements can present this way and require clinical evaluation
Not a substitute for addressing a real total-sleep-duration deficit if one is also present — check this rule alongside duration/recovery signals, not in isolation

estimated_impact.sleep_quality: Mild to moderate improvement (dependent on identifying and addressing the actual cause)

learning_resources.title: Non-Sleep Deep Rest (NSDR) — Huberman Lab official page
Master Your Sleep & Be More Alert When Awake — Huberman Lab

evidence_metadata.scientific_rationale: Two-signal combination: restless_periods > 130% of baseline AND sleep_duration >= 95% of baseline, both for one night. The combination is designed specifically to distinguish 'fragmented but long-enough' sleep from 'short' sleep, since the two call for different responses (investigate a cause vs. sleep more) and the recovery-deficit rule family already covers the short-sleep case.

evidence_for_protocol.notes: That fragmented sleep commonly traces to identifiable proximate causes (alcohol, late caffeine, environment, pre-sleep arousal) is well supported in the general sleep science literature, though this specific app does not cite a Huberman Lab episode that frames 'restlessness with adequate duration' as its own category the way it does for NSDR or light timing. The NSDR fallback action is direct_evidence on its own (see recovery-deficit.json); the 'investigate causes' framing as the primary action is evidence-informed rather than a direct single-source citation.

evidence_for_trigger.notes: The 130%-of-baseline restlessness threshold, the 95%-of-baseline duration floor, and the AND combination are all product heuristics chosen to approximate 'duration is fine but sleep felt broken up' — none are independently validated cutoffs. The duration floor in particular is a judgment call (95% was chosen to mean 'not meaningfully short,' not 'exactly average') that should be tuned against real outcome and self-report data once available.

expected_effect.short_term: No same-night effect (this fires the morning after); the reflection step may prevent a repeat the following night if a specific cause is identified and addressed.
expected_effect.long_term: If a recurring specific cause is found and addressed, expected to reduce restless-period frequency over subsequent weeks; untested as a rule in this app.
